title: Introduce 'cost-lens' per-invocation decomposition and conditional span augmentation
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a low-cardinality, high-value view into per-invocation cost and latency composition to support diagnosing expensive outliers and to reduce alert noise. This PR introduces 'cost-lens', a runtime-side aggregation that produces compact per-invocation decomposition (model compute, kv-cache miss cost, fallback/variant cost, I/O overhead) and a conditional OTEL span augmentation pipeline that attaches enriched attributes only when an invocation crosses configurable cost/latency thresholds.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a new cost-lens aggregator that emits a single compact JSON blob per invocation with normalized cost buckets and a short invocation fingerprint for joinability. The blob is intended for downstream rollups and on-demand drilldowns.
- Implements a span_enricher module (runtime and adapter) that conditionally decorates traces with cost-lens attributes when: cost > tenant-configured threshold OR latency SLO is violated OR invocation matches an anomaly rule. This keeps span cardinality low.
- Exposes a lightweight sampling heuristic and a deterministic fallback to ensure reproducible enrichment for reruns and replayed traces.
- Adds a Console dashboard panel definition (observability/cost_lens_panel.json) showing: per-invocation breakdown, 95/99 cost cohorts, and a small waterfall visualization for selected invocations.
- Adds guidance and a default alert tuning recipe to reduce long-tail alert storms by combining cost-lens-derived anomaly-scoring with our existing SLO gates.

Implementation details:
- Runtime aggregator implemented in runtimes/telemetry/cost_lens/aggregator.go. The aggregator attaches a minimal invocation_fingerprint (8-byte base64) and cost_buckets ([compute, cache_miss, fallback, io]) with normalized token counts and estimated GPU-ms.
- OTEL span enricher implemented in runtimes/telemetry/span_enricher/processor.py. Enrichment is conditional: attributes are added only when enrichment_criteria() returns true. We added unit and integration tests to validate conditional behavior and schema compatibility.
- Console: observability/cost_lens_panel.json contains Vega-lite specs and a compact SQL for the rollup backend. Panel uses sampled_span_join_key to fetch enrichment blobs for drilldown without increasing cardinality in primary traces.
- Backwards compatibility: enrichment attributes are optional and have fallbacks. We added a migration for older traces to ignore unknown attributes.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime aggregator + tests
- [x] Span enricher + schema validation
- [x] Console panel and dashboard docs
- [x] Default alert tuning recipe and examples
- [x] Performance benchmark (micro): observed +0.45% p99 CPU on a medium throughput serving host when enrichment is idle; +1.8% when enrichment triggered at 1% sampling.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag telemetry.cost_lens.enabled (off by default).
- Canary rollout to dev->staging for 48 hours, then gradual ramp to 5%, 20%, 100% tenant coverage with monitoring on enrichment rate and cardinality metrics.

Notes and caveats:
- Because the enricher can attach additional attributes, we limit attribute cardinality by hashing and clipping values and only attaching short fingerprints.
- The panel relies on a new compact rollup; users with long retention may need storage config changes (documented in the PR).

References: Linear ENG-2109 for the dashboard work, ENG-2331 for sampling heuristics. Related incident SUP-4421 motivated the conditional enrichment thresholding approach.
